elements.element: Customer may terminate the Agreement or an Order Form for convenience.
elements.evidence: New Section 7.7: "The Issuer (the "Customer" for the Servicer's services) may terminate this Agreement and the Servicer's rights and obligations under this Agreement for convenience...". There are no Order Forms in this transaction structure, so agreement-level termination suffices. The deterministic check "Customer convenience termination present" returned false only because the operative subject is styled "The Issuer (the "Customer"...)" rather than the bare word "Customer"; in substance the Customer-side convenience right is present and unconditional.

elements.element: Customer's convenience termination requires no more than 30 days' written notice.
elements.evidence: Section 7.7: "upon thirty (30) days' prior written notice to the Servicer" — exactly 30 days, written, and no additional condition or consent gate.

elements.element: Vendor refunds prepaid fees pro rata after Customer's convenience termination.
elements.evidence: Section 7.7: "the Servicer will refund to the Customer pro rata any fees prepaid for the period after the effective date of the termination." Both the express "pro rata" basis and the post-effective-date period are stated (not merely inferred from a period-based refund).

elements.element: Vendor has no right to terminate for convenience during a committed term.
elements.evidence: Retained Section 7.1: "The Servicer will not resign as Servicer under this Agreement unless it determines it is legally unable to perform its obligations under this Agreement." The only other exit is the Indenture Trustee's for-cause removal on a continuing Servicer Termination Event (Section 7.2(c)). No Vendor-side convenience exit exists; Section 7.1 is untouched by the redline.

elements.element: Customer may terminate for convenience on 60 to 90 days' notice.
elements.evidence: Section 7.7 sets thirty (30) days, which is below the 60–90 day fallback band. This is a deliberate (and more favourable) preferred-level term, so the fallback level is simply not the level targeted.

elements.element: Any early-termination fee is capped at three months of fees.
elements.evidence: Condition does not apply: neither the original text nor Section 7.7 imposes any early-termination fee, penalty, instalment or contingent payment on the Issuer's exit, so there is no fee requiring a cap.

elements.element: Vendor may terminate for convenience only at the end of a term.
elements.evidence: Satisfied a fortiori: Section 7.1 bars Servicer resignation entirely absent legal inability, so the Servicer has no convenience exit at any time, term-end or otherwise.

elements.element: Vendor must give at least 90 days' notice of convenience termination.
elements.evidence: Condition does not apply: the Servicer holds no convenience termination right at all under retained Section 7.1, so no notice period needs to be specified.

reasons: Preferred level is complete on the operative text: Section 7.7 supplies an unconditional Customer (Issuer) convenience right at 30 days' written notice with an express pro rata refund of prepaid fees, and retained Section 7.1 leaves the Servicer with no convenience exit during the term.

The failed regex "Customer convenience termination present" is a naming artifact, not a substantive gap — the right is granted to "The Issuer (the "Customer" for the Servicer's services)" in Section 7.7.

Minimality holds: three operations only (insert Section 7.7; add the Section 7.7 exit to Section 8.3; reletter (a)/(b)/(c) and change "earlier" to "earliest"). The Section 8.3 conforming edit is necessary because Section 8.3's exhaustive termination list would otherwise contradict the new exit. No survival tails, expense language, damages categories or unrelated deletions were added; Section 7.1 and Section 7.2(c) are untouched.

Intent is not preserved: by routing the new exit through Section 8.3(a), a unilateral 30-day notice from the Issuer terminates the entire multi-party Transfer and Servicing Agreement — not just the servicing engagement — while Notes remain Outstanding and Receivables unserviced. Repair: scope Section 7.7 (and the new Section 8.3(a)) to termination of the Servicer's appointment/servicing role rather than of "this Agreement", or expressly preserve the Agreement as to the Depositor, Custodian and Marketing Agent roles.

Related contradiction to repair in operative language: the defined term "Servicer" means "Cellco or any Successor Servicer engaged under Section 7.4 of the Transfer and Servicing Agreement", and Sections 7.3/7.4 presuppose the Agreement continuing so a Successor Servicer can be engaged and transition performed. If Section 8.3(a) terminates the Agreement on the Issuer's notice, that machinery is inoperative. Either tie the effective date of the Section 7.7 termination to the appointment of a Successor Servicer under Section 7.4 (a timing mechanic, not a consent condition, so the election remains unconditional), or add an express carve-out that Sections 7.3 and 7.4 continue to apply to a Section 7.7 termination.

Drafting nit (not a level failure): Section 7.7 coins the term "Customer" solely for use within that section; confirm it does not collide with any other defined term and consider using "the Issuer" throughout to avoid an orphan definition. Also note that the Servicing Fee is paid monthly out of collections, so the prepaid-fee refund will rarely bite — harmless, but the exit's value rests on the termination right itself.
